source.title: TaxoSAE: Rethinking Sparse Autoencoders through Taxonomic Logic
source.authors: Xin-Yu Guo; Minglai Yang; Clayton T. Morrison; Eduardo Blanco; Mihai Surdeanu

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures how concepts are distributed across SAE features and how well SAE features support concept readout. It refines the scope of claims about SAE features as representation units, but does not test toy-model superposition or its geometry.
record.gate_note: The relevant results measure feature concentration in supervised TaxoSAE and unsupervised SAE baselines, and report readout results. The paper's descriptions of prior work are not treated as results. Results on swaps, ablations and unseen concepts are not included as rows here; the concentration metrics are the most direct measures of feature units for these claim versions.
record.test_reason: This is a method paper. It proposes TaxoSAE, a supervised, stacked SAE that binds each taxonomy concept to a designated slot, and compares it with unsupervised SAE baselines on two small, fine-tuned factual-QA taxonomies. TaxoSAE's concentration (EffFeat about 1, Top1C about 90–100%) is produced by explicit supervised binding. It therefore says nothing about whether SAE features found without supervision are the model's natural units (V5), or whether real models contain recoverable sparse features (V4). The unsupervised SAE numbers are baselines for the method comparison, not a designed test of any version. No toy models, capacity, polysemanticity or feature dimensionality are studied (V1–V3, V6). The study relies on SAEs as a tool and reports its own method's performance against them, so it does not test the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that existing SAEs learn a flat feature space with no taxonomic consistency for readout and no granularity for control. They conclude that TaxoSAE (stacked SAEs plus a taxonomic alignment loss) gives more accurate readout, more precise control and readout of unseen concepts at their hypernyms. They note the limits of English-only experiments and simple three-level taxonomies. They draw no conclusion about superposition itself.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains supervised, stacked SAEs with taxonomic alignment on fine-tuned LLM activations. It does not use the original toy-network superposition setup or measure overlapping feature directions.
record.method_sensitivity: Representation results depend on the SAE method and supervision: TaxoSAE is much more concentrated than the unsupervised baselines. The paper also reports layer-dependent steering performance; the main experiments use layer 6 for Bio and layer 9 for Animal, and layer 12 for Qwen Bio.

fits_no_version.finding: Unsupervised SAEs (10k ReLU features, trained on fine-tuned GPT-2 small / Qwen2.5-0.5B last-token activations) spread each taxonomy concept's mean activation over many features: EffFeat 133–645, Top1C 1.3–7.5% (Tables 1, 4). DiffMean-selected single features read concepts at 22–82% diagonal accuracy. Caveat: the metric is averaged over all features on questions that also encode a second element (person or property).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In unsupervised SAEs on small fine-tuned LMs, a single dictionary feature captures only a small share of a taxonomic concept's activation (concept fragmentation across features).

record.problems: The models are fine-tuned separately on small, controlled English factual-QA datasets; TaxoSAE receives explicit concept and taxonomy supervision. The concentration results therefore do not establish natural or general LLM feature units. The paper reports a single seed for Qwen results and no uncertainty estimates for the Table 1/Table 4 concentration values.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports additional activation-concentration values for Random Unsup. SAE and Hybrid SAE, readout accuracies, selectivity, swaps, and unseen-concept results (Tables 1, 2, 4, 7; Figs. 3–6). Random Unsup. SAE concentration duplicates DiffMean because the methods share dictionaries; Hybrid results and the other metrics are not included here to keep the catalog rows focused on the direct concentration comparison.

untested.parts: No toy networks, sparsity sweep, phase transition or geometry.
No neuron polysemanticity or capacity competition.
No designed test of distributed or SAE-recoverable features in LLMs. Unsupervised SAEs appear only as baselines with post-hoc DiffMean selection.
No test of completeness, stability or canonicity of SAE features found without supervision. The supervised TaxoSAE concentration is by construction.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T5' and its V4/V5 labels are not supported. TaxoSAE's concentration comes from supervised slot binding, and the unsupervised numbers are baseline comparators. It is also unclear whether TaxoSAE's EffFeat/Top1C are computed over the same unit set as the unsupervised SAEs' 10k features. Hybrid SAE shares TaxoSAE's L1 values, which suggests the measure for TaxoSAE covers bind slots only. That makes the comparison not like-for-like. Random and DiffMean concentration values are identical by construction.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, feature-over-dimension sweep, superposition transition, or overlapping-direction geometry is tested.
No neuron polysemanticity or competition for limited representational capacity is tested.
No alternative causes of polysemantic neurons are tested.

The study tests SAE feature concentration and concept readout in fine-tuned models on two small factual QA taxonomies. It does not test neuron-level feature spreading or general LLM representations without fine-tuning and task-specific supervision.
The study measures concentration and readout in its tested SAEs, but does not test whether features are stable across broad model, dataset, or training changes, or establish canonical completeness.
No dimensionality or direction geometry of superposed features is measured.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: TaxoSAE on the tested fine-tuned GPT-2 small and Qwen2.5-0.5B factual-QA taxonomies
reader_labels.reason: The task-supervised TaxoSAE concentrates concepts into roughly one feature and the authors report accurate concept readout; concentration metrics support SAE-recoverable concepts in these settings (C02,C04,C06,C14,C16,C18,C26,C28,C30).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Unsupervised DiffMean SAE dictionaries on the tested taxonomies
reader_labels.reason: Concept activations are highly fragmented in these dictionaries, so the results do not support reliable recovery of each concept as a concentrated feature without task-specific alignment (C01,C03,C05,C13,C15,C17,C25,C27,C29).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Unsupervised DiffMean SAE dictionaries on Bio and Animal
reader_labels.reason: The reported effective feature counts and Top1C values show that these unsupervised SAE features are not single, concentrated units for the tested concepts (C01,C03,C05,C07,C09,C11,C13,C15,C17,C19,C21,C23,C25,C27,C29,C31,C33,C35).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: TaxoSAE obtains concentrated features after explicit concept binding and taxonomic supervision; this demonstrates concentration under the designed method, not that SAE features are generally canonical or stable (C02,C04,C06,C08,C10,C12,C14,C16,C18,C20,C22,C24,C26,C28,C30,C32,C34,C36).
